builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG
summary: Replaces prompting a generative LLM for RAG knowledge-conflict classification with typed decision models that return probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass, optionally cascading low-confidence cases to a frontier model. Costs are minimal—4–39x lower billed cost than Gemini 2.5 Flash and 2.6–6.0x lower latency—while adding model-serving complexity and a confidence threshold. Can fail on planted false sources where decision models are less reliable as hard labels, and decomposing the taxonomy into yes/no questions or transferring repairs across models degrades accuracy.
rationale: The method is immediately deployable via commercial inference APIs, demonstrably cheaper and faster than the baseline LLM approach with no loss in downstream behavioural accuracy, and requires no infrastructure beyond API access.
technique: Decision-model cascade for RAG conflict typing

claims.statement: Replaces prompting a generative LLM for RAG knowledge-conflict classification with typed decision models that return probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass, optionally cascading low-confidence cases to a frontier model. Costs are minimal—4–39x lower billed cost than Gemini 2.5 Flash and 2.6–6.0x lower latency—while adding model-serving complexity and a confidence threshold. Can fail on planted false sources where decision models are less reliable as hard labels, and decomposing the taxonomy into yes/no questions or transferring repairs across models degrades accuracy.

Ten of eleven decision models match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash accuracy (61.3%) at 4–39x lower billed cost and 2.6–6.0x lower latency; cascading the least confident quarter to Gemini 3.8 Flash achieves statistical parity at 25–37% of its cost.
